title: Part 9
html:
The Sabarmati and two Bengalis. Ghogha and the courtesan Barmukhi. Ruined Somnath. Junagadh and Girnar: Dattatreya's footprints and the story of Krishna's footprints (pp. 163–182)

[p. 163]

1780"He is not a pandit who prides himself on learning,
if his heart has not been purified by the rasa of devotion.

1781One who counts millions of universes as straw
and is drunk with love — him I accept as a devotee.

1782Love and devotion are the essence of truth, so the shrutis say;
the devotee of Hari, drunk with love, does not want liberation.

1783One for whom love and devotion are the ornament of his throat
is an eternal associate of Krishna.

1784One who tastes the sweetness1 of love for Krishna —
him I will serve at his feet without dispute.

1785One who, in this very body, has cut his bonds
and is drunk with love for Krishna — he is a thakura.

1786Mahamaya, throwing dust into the eye of knowledge,
has tied a knot between consciousness and matter.

1787That is why the foolish in this world,
deluded, identify the self with the inert body.

1788One who gives up identification with the inert body
is my master — so the Vedas say.

1789The supreme Vaishnava, immersed in love for Krishna,
does not dissemble by making a great noise.

1790One who does not know the primary meaning of Vedanta
regards the jiva and Brahman as one."

[p. 164]

1791Saying this, the next day Gora, the delight of hearts,
left the town and went west.

1792Going a little way, we saw the river Shubhramati,2
singing with a murmuring voice, full of rasa.

1793Crossing the river, we saw two or four people
going to Dvaraka on pilgrimage.

1794Among them I saw two Bengalis —
great devotees, Ramananda and Govinda Charana.

1795Seeing people from Gauda after so long,
my heart seemed to dance with joy.

1796I asked Ramananda, "Where is your home?"
Ramananda said, "Brother, in Kulina-gram."3

1797The Lord is bathing in the river Shubhramati,
and meanwhile Ramananda is talking with me.

1798Ramananda said, "Where are you going?"
I said, "I am going with the Lord to Dvaraka."

1799Ramananda, hearing Chaitanyadeva's name,
lit up in the face like a flash of lightning.

1800Ramananda ran and bowed down,
and Chaitanya asked him a few questions.

1801Ramananda Dasa is a supreme Vaishnava;
the Lord gave Ramananda Dasa encouragement.

[p. 165]

1802The Lord said, "Ramananda, seeing you,
the feeling of Gauda has awakened in my heart.

1803How long ago did you leave home?
How long ago did you come to this holy land?

1804Come then, let us go together to Dvaraka,
and all of us joyfully behold the Lord of Dvaraka."

1805Hearing this from the Lord's lips, Ramananda Dasa
rejoiced to stay with the Lord.

1806Having bathed, the Lord walks slowly on
and arrives at a village called Ghogha.

1807A courtesan named Barmukhi4 lives here;
there is no telling of her treasures.

1808By her trade she has amassed great wealth;
her clothes and ornaments are very costly.

1809Barmukhi lives in a huge house
and goes about by every trick to rob the rich of their wealth.

1810Wearing [fine clothes], she looks about languidly;
how many libertines go to her house!

1811She lives here with many servants and maids;
everyone knows of her pomp and fame.

1812There is a huge garden called Piyar-kanan;5
the Lord went to the edge of that garden.

[p. 166]

1813A very large neem tree stands here;
who knows why, but the Lord went and sat there.

1814At his command I go to householders' doors
to beg for fruits, roots and the like.

1815Having begged, I came back at midday,
and the Lord made the offering with a joyful heart.

1816Then the three of us received the prasada —
I, Ramananda and Govinda Charana.

1817Laughing, I called Govinda my "mite".6
The Lord said, "Why do you leave Ramananda out?

1818If Govinda has become your mite,
then Ramananda shall be my mite."

1819Laughing, he called Ramananda his mite,
and began the Name, clapping his hands.

1820Ramananda, hearing this from the Lord's lips,
stood to one side, rubbing his hands in embarrassment.

1821Many people gathered to hear the Name,
and tears flowed from the Lord's eyes in a hundred streams.

1822The tears began to spurt like a squirt-gun,
and seeing this the people of Ghogha were amazed.

1823Seeing that Hari-sankirtana of the Lord,
two or four people became drunk with love.

[p. 167]

1824Tears flow from the eyes of the village people;
many people came and stood in rows.

1825What a mood of devotion it was cannot be described;
without blinking they all gaze at the Lord's face.

1826Sometimes the Lord laughs, sometimes he weeps,
sometimes, raising his arms, he dances and sings.

1827Sometimes he trembles all over and sweat flows,
sometimes in an ecstasy of love he remains silent.

1828Sometimes he totters, his hair on end,
sometimes he calls aloud, "Krishna, my life!"

1829"The young sannyasi is drunk with love of God" —
so the people of Ghogha whisper to one another.

1830As he says "Hari, Hari", streams of bliss flow;
all stand there like puppets.

1831His eyes half-closed, his matted hair loosened,
his body smeared with dust and grime.

1832"Where is Krishna, my life?" he calls,
sometimes raising his hands and gazing upwards.

1833"Govinda, where is Krishna? Bring him to me!
Where is Krishna, my life? Show him to me!"

1834Once, saying this, he ran off
and, spreading his arms, embraced the neem tree.

[p. 168]

1835Nimai became drunk with love of God;
never have I seen such madness.

1836For many days I have been with him, wandering through many lands,
but never have I seen such ecstasy.

1837Ramananda and Govinda Charana on either side
clapped their hands and raised the cry of "Hari" again and again.

1838At the roadside there was a huge pit,
and in his ecstasy he rolled down into it.

1839A wicked man came along, bustling about,
and said to the Lord, "Why are you deceiving people?

1840You will fool the village people and take their money;
that is why you go about shouting 'Hari'.

1841I have come to test the sannyasi;
I have seen hundreds of false sannyasis."

1842When that unbeliever said this,
the village people wanted to thrash him.

1843The Lord said, "Brothers, whom will you beat?
Make him drink the nectar of the Name of Hari.

1844His throat has dried up with thirst;
pour a stream of nectar into his mouth.

1845Without devotion his heart has withered;
give him the Name and destroy his fear of Yama.

[p. 169]

1846The unbeliever's heart is like a desert;
give it the power to bear fruit.

1847Come to me, holy man, I will give you the Name of Hari;
I will lift the burden of your sins from you.

1848By the power of this mantra all suffering will go;
reciting the mantra of the Name of Hari bears fruit at once.

1849One who recites this great mantra —
that sinner never goes to hell.

1850When there is such an easy mantra in the world,
why should the sinner wander uselessly on evil paths?"

1851Saying this, Mahaprabhu went up to him
and poured the nectar of the Name of Hari into his ears.

1852Merciful Chaitanya, to deliver living beings,
wanders here and there, undisturbed.

1853Seeing all this from her window,
Barmukhi pondered within herself.

1854Having seen the Lord's wondrous mercy with her own eyes,
sitting alone, she reproached herself.

1855Barmukhi said, "For shame, for shame! For the sake of money
I sell my body a hundred times a day.

1856By sinful trade, uniting with other men —
for shame! — every day I indulge in amorous play.

[p. 170]

1857This sannyasi I see is equal to God;
I will leave everything and go to him.

1858The sannyasi has no money or cowries with him —
why then am I happy when I see him?

1859Why should I suffer hell sitting at home?
Will Hari not have mercy on me too?

1860What mantra did this sannyasi recite into the ear of Balaji the villain,7
that he delivered him?

1861I will go to him and destroy my sins;
I will go up to him and clasp his feet tightly."

1862So Barmukhi spoke from the window,
and everyone was glad to hear her words.

1863The people all around, taking up the news,
made a great commotion, laughing.

1864A moment later the courtesan came down,
and her maid named Mira went behind her.

1865Then Barmukhi said humbly to Mira,
"From today I give all my wealth to you.

1866I have much money — I count it all as nothing;
from today I have become a beggar on the road."

1867Barmukhi, the maidservant,8 let down her hair,
like a bank of clouds beside motionless lightning.

[p. 171]

1868The long net of her hair falls below her hips,
while Shachi's darling sits with his eyes closed.

1869All, seeing the wondrous radiance of her beauty,
stand gazing at her face.

1870Barmukhi, with folded hands, says again and again,
"Cut my bonds, my sannyasi.

1871I am a great sinner, a worm of hell;
if you do not have mercy, I shall go to perdition.

1872Tell your maidservant by what means I shall be saved,
how, after death, I shall escape the fear of Yama.

1873What further use have I for this sinful body?"
Saying this, she cut off her long hair.

1874Putting on simple clothes, she covered her nakedness
and stood before the Lord with folded hands.

1875The Lord said, "Barmukhi, I will tell you
a few words — carry them out in every respect.

1876Make a tulasi grove here,
and living in its midst, practise the worship of Krishna."

1877"You are Krishna, you are Hari," said Barmukhi,
and saying just this she fell at the Lord's feet.

1878When Barmukhi fell at his feet,
the Lord at once drew back three or four steps.

[p. 172]

1879And all the other people standing near
cried, "Blessed, blessed!" on seeing the courtesan.

1880The maid Mirabai wept bitterly,
and Barmukhi said to her with a smile:

1881"Listen carefully, Mira, to my words:
I have given you all the wealth I have.

1882Serve guests well when they come;
in solitude, set your mind on the Name of Hari.

1883Do no sinful deeds — I adjure you;
worship Sri Radha-Krishna with loving attachment.

1884To love is good indeed, but not with a rogue;
make your love with Krishna, Mira.

1885Give body, mind and life — everything — to Krishna;
then you will gain Krishna, the eternal treasure.

1886Listen carefully to what I say, Mira:
keep company with no one but Krishna.

1887Krishna will surely be merciful to you;
never, at any cost, give up the treasure that is Krishna.

1888By the Lord's mercy my bonds are cut;
from today my dwelling is the tulasi grove."

1889Saying this, Barmukhi took her chanting beads
and made a tulasi grove, forgetting all her pain.

[p. 173]

1890Having given devotion to the courtesan Barmukhi,
the Lord hurried off to see Somnath.

1891The Lord goes in the direction of Jafarabad,
and with great difficulty arrives there in three days.

1892The people of Jafarabad are very poor,
yet they show great honour to guests.

1893Many villagers brought alms,
and my Lord made rotis and offered them.

1894Going into a gardener's garden,
we spent the night there happily.

1895Rising in the morning, we go to Somnath
and, after six days, arrive there.

1896There is none of its former beauty, nor that temple;
seeing its sorry state, tears flowed from my eyes.

1897Heaps of rubble and broken remains are there;
seeing them, I felt a great pain in my heart.

1898The beauty of the temple buildings has gone;
seeing this, my Lord weeps in distress.

1899Weeping, my Lord began to say,
"What has the wicked Yavana9 done here!

1900Where have you hidden, Lord, for fear of the Yavanas?
Show yourself once and soothe my heart."

[p. 174]

1901Alas, alas, this sorrow is beyond words;
Gora Raya weeps, calling on Somnath.

1902The Lord said, "Who carried off such splendour?
For money's sake the villain brought it to this.

1903O Lord Somnath, to see you
my heart is in turmoil — I cannot bear it.

1904I can bear separation from you no longer;
calling on you, my heart is breaking.

1905Alas, alas, what sin did the devotees commit,
for what sin do they no longer see you, O god?

1906In separation from you hundreds of pandas10
are sunk in an ocean of sorrow.

1907Did you go to Kailasa for fear of the Yavanas
and now forget your dear devotees?

1908Seeing all this my heart is bursting,
and tears stream down onto my breast.

1909Ah, only ruins are left lying here —
how can sinful eyes bear it?

1910Come, Lord Somnath, into my heart;
in my heart I shall behold your form.

1911Where have you hidden, Lord? I do not see you.
To whom shall I tell how my soul feels?

[p. 175]

1912Alas, alas, Gangadhara! To see you
people will no longer come from foreign lands.

1913Pilgrims used to come to see you with pride,
but now that glory has been wiped away.

1914The Yavanas in their hatred, committing outrages,
have carried off gems, pearls and other riches.

1915Alas, Lord Smarahara,11 where have you stayed?
In your mercy you do not show yourself to your devotees."

1916Thus my Lord lamented,
and just then a storm arose in the sky.

1917Dust flew up and darkened all around,
and the pandas shut the doors of their huts.

1918We all sat by the outer door,
and the Lord, the Hari-bola, came and sat in our midst.

1919Just then an avadhuta sannyasi came
and looked again and again at Gora-chand.

1920His whole body smeared with ash, no cloth,
his matted hair tied up high, of wondrous form.

1921His two eyes are red,
"Hara, Hara" on his lips, his heart pure.

1922Two languid eyes, beautiful to see;
he came and blessed him with raised hand.12

[p. 176]

1923Seeing him, my Lord rose,
and he, saying something, vanished.

1924Where the avadhuta went, he was seen no more.
Then, with a slight smile, my Chaitanya

1925walked three times around Somnath.
I, Ramananda and Govinda Charana

1926sing Hari-sankirtana with the Lord;
for the pleasure of Thakura Somnath

1927the Lord sings kirtana, melting with love.
Two or four pandas came and joined us

1928and began asking us for something.
Smiling, the Lord said, "A sannyasi

1929has no money, cowries, food or cloth to give."
Hearing these words, Govinda Charana

1930placed two coins in the panda's hand.
The panda took us to the edge of the holy tank,

1931and my Lord took water and poured it on his head.
Leaving Somnath, we go to Junagadh.13

1932A large place indeed, but there is no tirtha;
many mansions stand in splendour all around.

1933In Junagadh Gora Raya spent two days.

[p. 177]

1934In one place there is the worship of Ranchhodji;
in the evening we go there for darshan.

1935An excellent brahmana named Miraji performs the service;
we go and arrive at his house.

1936Miraji received us with devotion,
and the Lord spent the night at his house.

1937The brahmana brings milk, sugar and flour,
and the Lord spends the night joyfully.

1938Nearby is the most charming Girnar hill;14
Lord Vishvambhara goes towards it.

1939Miraji, coming up with devotion,
asks the Lord again and again to stay.

1940Humbly the Lord says to the brahmana,
"We shall all go to Girnar hill.

1941There I shall see the feet of Guru Dattatreya;
let me go — that is the alms I ask of you."

1942Hearing the Lord's words, the worthy brahmana
said nothing more, good or bad.

1943Chaitanya Gosai sets out,
and we follow behind him like shadows.

1944A band of sannyasis had come to this place
and were sitting with gloomy faces.

[p. 178]

1945Their leader, named Bhargadeva,
had fallen ill and was staying there.

1946Bhargadeva is tossing about beneath a tree;
the Lord came there quickly.

1947Seeing Bhargadeva ill, Gora Raya
orders me to look after him.

1948I, Ramananda and Govinda Charana —
the three of us set to nursing the sick man.

1949The Lord tells us to give him neem juice to drink,
and we make neem juice and give it to him.

1950Freed from his illness, Bhargadeva
bows countless times at the Lord's feet.

1951Bhargadeva rises and praises the Lord;
rubbing his hands, Bharga says with devotion:

1952"Have mercy on me, Lord, you are merciful;
my heart is eager for you.

1953You have freed this lowly one from disease;
in your mercy cut the noose of maya too.

1954Whom are you deceiving, young sannyasi?
I long to attain your feet.

1955If you have no mercy on the lowly,
why should I call you merciful?

[p. 179]

1956I am old, and my eyes deceive me:
in your heart I see a golden doll.

1957Everyone says your colour is golden,
but my eyes see you dark, like Krishna.

1958That is why I say my eyes are faulty;
in your mercy deliver this sinner."15

1959In his mercy the Lord infused power into Bharga,
and at once devotion welled up in his heart.

1960What the Lord said to Bhargadeva with a wink is not known,
but at once tears flowed from his eyes.

1961The sannyasi's disciples did not grasp the subtle truth,
while Bharga went with the Lord to Girnar.

1962Girnar hill is very high;
the two feet of Guru Dattatreya are there.

1963On the high summit of Girnar are the two feet;
the band of sannyasis goes to see the feet.

1964In the morning we set out to see the feet,
and in the afternoon we reach the feet.

1965Two footprints stand out on a rock;
seeing the feet, the Lord bowed down.

1966Flag, thunderbolt and goad adorn the soles;16
seeing the lotus feet, the Lord says "Hari, Hari".

[p. 180]

1967A panda lives here permanently;
Vishvambhara asks him about the feet.

1968The panda said, "When the Yadus perished,
then Baladeva came here.

1969Baladeva came here for austerity;
the Lord took his yogic seat and began his austerities.

1970Baladeva sat in austerity in his yogic posture,
while at Prabhasa the Yadavas began to fight.

1971Drunk on mead, all the heroes
fought one another, and blood flowed.

1972Satyaki and all the other heroes
one by one went to the abode of Yama.

1973By Krishna's will all the Yadus perished,
and at last Krishna appeared on the mountain.

1974Here, seeing Baladeva, the Lord of the Yadus
began to speak of his own departure.

1975Krishna says to Baladeva, 'I shall go to Goloka;
my work is accomplished, I shall stay no longer.

1976The earth has been filled with the sins of the Yadavas,
and that is why the Yadus have been destroyed.

1977If the sons of Pandu weep for me,
you will relieve their grief.

[p. 181]

1978Drupada's daughter is dearer to me than life;
I beg you, comfort her first.'

1979Hearing this, Baladeva burst into tears
and humbly said these words:

1980'Vidura, Uddhava and all the other devotees —
what shall I tell them when you are gone?

1981Leave some sign for them,
seeing which they will be filled with love.

1982You are their very life — knowing and understanding this,
how can you go to Goloka?

1983They know nothing but Krishna;
how can you abandon them and go to your own abode?

1984When Panchali raises her cry of grief,
what shall I say to console her? Consider it yourself.'

1985Hearing this, Krishna set his feet here,
and at once the footprints remained here."

1986When the panda had explained this,
love at once arose in the Lord's heart.

1987Gora, the abode of bliss, the home of love,
gazes steadily at the footprints.

1988As he gazed at the prints, a waterfall of love
suddenly overflowed in his heart.

[p. 182]

1989Choked with feeling, the Lord says slowly,
"Brother panda, you are a holy man; what a jewel you have shown!

1990Every day you gain happiness from seeing them;
I see no one as virtuous as you.

1991If this print were to fall on a heart of stone,
the bliss of Brahman would arise in it every day."

1992Laying his head on the footprint, Gora, the delight of hearts,
falls prostrate on it again and again.

1993His body, thin as a cane,
swelled with love, finding its chance.

1994Touching the feet, the Lord closed his eyes,
and tears began to flow down his breast.

1995He circles the feet, clapping his hands,
and his waist-cloth and the knot of his hair slipped loose.

1996Seeing this state, Ramananda lost consciousness,
and Govinda Charana fell rolling on the ground.

1997Coming down from the mountain, my Gora Raya
spends the night on the bank of the river called Bhadra.

1998Rising in the morning, we all cross the river
and gradually come in sight of the Dhanvidhara thickets.

1999The Dhanvidhara thickets are very extensive;
seeing those thickets, I was afraid.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Shikharini is a sweet dish of yogurt with sugar; a metaphor of sweetness.
  2. Shubhramati is the Sabarmati.
  3. Kulina-gram is a village in Bardhaman, home of Ramananda Vasu and other associates of Chaitanya.
  4. The episode of the courtesan Barmukhi (Bar-mukhi) is one of the best known in the Karcha.
  5. Piyar-kanan, literally "garden of love".
  6. Mite (mita): a sworn friend, a bosom companion. A joking play on names: Govinda is the author's namesake, and Ramananda is the namesake of Ramananda Raya, Chaitanya's friend.
  7. Apparently the name of the villain of the preceding episode, Balaji.
  8. "Maidservant" here in the sense of "maidservant of the Lord": Barmukhi already calls herself so.
  9. Yavana: a foreigner, a Muslim. Somnath was destroyed by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025 and repeatedly thereafter.
  10. Pandas are temple priests and pilgrim guides.
  11. Smarahara, "destroyer of Kama", is an epithet of Shiva. Gangadhara, "bearer of the Ganga", is also an epithet of Shiva.
  12. A passage is repeated here in the edition (pp. 175–176); the repetition is omitted.
  13. From this point the lines in the edition appear to be out of order (the couplets are broken); the translation follows the order of the lines.
  14. Girnar (Gunagarh) is the sacred mountain at Junagadh, a place of worship of Dattatreya.
  15. Compare the similar episode with another Bharga in Part 5.
  16. Flag, thunderbolt (vajra) and goad (ankusha) are auspicious marks on the feet of God.
